question: What is the main goal of Essential Obstetric Care (EOC)?

options.A: Reducing the overall cost of hospital-based maternity services
options.B: Ensuring every birth occurs in a tertiary specialist hospital
options.C: Providing routine antenatal health education to community groups
options.D: Preventing and managing life-threatening maternal and neonatal complications

explanation: Essential Obstetric Care is all about those life-saving interventions that keep both mother and baby safe during pregnancy, birth, and after delivery. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h1)

question: Why are maternal complications during childbirth considered so dangerous?

options.A: They only occur in women with a known history of chronic illness
options.B: They are completely preventable with strict bed rest during pregnancy
options.C: They usually respond slowly to standard emergency medical treatments
options.D: They develop suddenly and can quickly become fatal without prompt care

explanation: Complications like severe bleeding can start out of nowhere. That is why quick action from a skilled nurse is such a lifesaver! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h1)

question: How many signal functions must a health facility perform to be called a BEmOC center?
explanation: To be officially recognized as a Basic Emergency Obstetric Care (BEmOC) center, a facility must be able to handle all seven specific medical interventions. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h2)

question: A nurse gives an injection to stop heavy bleeding right after delivery. Which BEmOC signal function is this?
explanation: Spot on! Uterotonics like oxytocin are injectable drugs used to contract the uterus and stop postpartum bleeding. A key BEmOC skill! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h2)

question: What two extra services make a CEmOC facility different from a BEmOC facility?

options.A: Manual vacuum aspiration and neonatal bag-valve-mask ventilation
options.B: Administration of intravenous antibiotics and magnesium sulfate
options.C: Blood transfusion and emergency Caesarean section surgery
options.D: Routine antenatal ultrasound and postpartum family planning

explanation: While BEmOC covers seven basic functions, Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric Care (CEmOC) steps it up with blood transfusions and major surgeries like C-sections. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h3)

question: Why is having a blood transfusion service so important in a CEmOC facility?

options.A: To reduce the incidence of newborn jaundice following difficult deliveries
options.B: To prevent mild gestational anemia during routine antenatal clinic visits
options.C: To speed up cervical dilation during the active phase of normal labour
options.D: To replace severe blood loss from conditions like postpartum hemorrhage or placenta previa

explanation: When a mother loses too much blood, quick access to safe blood can literally mean the difference between life and death. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h3)

question: Which of these is a leading direct cause of maternal mortality?
explanation: Heavy bleeding after childbirth is one of the top direct causes of maternal death worldwide. Knowing how to spot and manage it is essential for every nursing student! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h4)

question: What are the main warning signs of severe pre-eclampsia during pregnancy?

options.A: Complete cessation of fetal movements felt by the mother for two days
options.B: Very high blood pressure accompanied by severe headache and visual changes
options.C: Sudden painless vaginal bleeding in the third trimester of pregnancy
options.D: High fever with generalized body chills and offensive vaginal discharge

explanation: Always watch out for high blood pressure paired with stubborn headaches or blurred vision—these are big red flags for pre-eclampsia! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h4)

question: Why do we tilt a pregnant woman in shock onto her left side during resuscitation?

options.A: To make it easier for the midwife to perform manual removal of the placenta
options.B: To encourage the rapid descent of the fetal head through the birth canal
options.C: To relieve pressure of the heavy uterus on major blood vessels and improve blood flow to the heart
options.D: To prevent the aspiration of stomach contents into the lungs during active seizures

explanation: The heavy womb can squash major blood vessels when she lies flat. Tilting her left keeps blood flowing smoothly back to her heart! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h5)

question: A postpartum patient is bleeding heavily and showing signs of shock. What is the most urgent vascular access step?

options.A: Insert two large-bore intravenous cannulas for rapid fluid replacement
options.B: Administer oral rehydration salts slowly through a nasogastric tube
options.C: Set up a single fine-needle peripheral line for routine daily hydration
options.D: Collect a midstream urine sample to check for urinary tract infection

explanation: In an emergency, large-bore IV lines let you pump in fluids and blood fast enough to rescue her blood pressure and beat shock. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h5)

question: At what cervical dilation does the active phase of normal labor officially start on a partograph?
explanation: 4 centimeters is your magic marker! That is where the active phase of labor officially begins on the partograph. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h6)

question: What should you do if a laboring woman's cervical dilation line crosses the action line on the partograph?

options.A: Waiting another four hours to see if contractions naturally pick up speed
options.B: Discharging the patient home to walk around until contractions become stronger
options.C: Stopping all forms of monitoring and allowing the patient to sleep undisturbed
options.D: Immediate medical intervention and preparation for emergency transfer or surgery

explanation: Crossing the action line means labor is not progressing normally. It is your cue to call for backup and get ready for urgent help or a C-section. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h6)

question: When is the right time for a nurse-midwife to practice hand hygiene in the labor ward?

options.A: Only at the beginning of the morning shift
options.B: Only after touching visible blood or amniotic fluid
options.C: Before and after every patient contact
options.D: After finishing all clinical duties for the day

explanation: Simple and non-negotiable: wash your hands or use sanitizer before and after every single patient touch to keep infections away. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h7)

question: Why do we use standard universal precautions for every single woman admitted to the labor ward?

options.A: Any patient can carry blood-borne infections even if their screening status is unknown
options.B: It saves time by eliminating the need to check laboratory test results
options.C: Pregnant women never develop secondary bacterial infections during birth
options.D: Government regulations only apply infection control to surgical patients

explanation: We treat all body fluids as infectious because in an emergency, we might not know a patient's status yet. Safety first for everyone! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h7)

question: What is a major transport-related challenge that often contributes to maternal deaths in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of fully equipped ambulances in villages
options.B: Too many doctors available at primary healthcare centers
options.C: Delays in transportation and reaching a medical facility
options.D: Immediate acceptance of patients at tertiary hospitals

explanation: Getting stuck trying to find transport to a hospital (the famous 'second delay') is a huge hurdle in saving mothers in remote areas. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h8)

question: What important step must a nurse take before transferring an obstetric emergency patient to a bigger hospital?

options.A: Wait until the patient's family fully pays all hospital bills in advance
options.B: Perform a major surgical operation at the primary clinic before transfer
options.C: Advise the patient to walk to the nearest main road to find a commercial taxi
options.D: Stabilize the patient's condition and write a clear referral note detailing care provided

explanation: Always stabilize what you can and write a clear handover note so the receiving team knows what has already been done! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h8)
